---
title: "Binary logistic regression verification record"
---

The [executed comparison](../notebooks/logistic-verification.qmd) fits identical
observations in base R `glm()`, statsmodels `Logit`, and PHP `fit_logistic_matrix()`.
The [saved report](logistic-results.json) records versions, complete outputs,
maximum differences from R, warnings and retained-row metadata.

## Reference cases and conventions

Six saved R fixtures cover the simulated learning sample, a single predictor,
multiple predictors, no intercept, intercept only, correlated full-rank columns
and imbalanced outcomes (the main sample is the multiple-predictor case).
The three-way comparison adds listwise deletion of two rows. All coefficients,
covariance entries, standard errors, normal z tests and p-values, Wald confidence
limits, full fitted probabilities and response residuals, likelihood, deviance,
null deviance, AIC and residual df are checked. Numerical tolerance is
1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference); sample accounting is exact.

R uses `confint.default(fit)`, not profile-likelihood `confint(fit)`.
Its fitting tolerance is 1e-14 to make covariance evaluated at the preceding
IRLS iterate negligible. Iteration counts can differ across implementations;
they are not a reference equality requirement. Without a ones column the null
baseline is probability 0.5; the Python runner computes this convention explicitly.

## Failure and integration checks

Rust/PHP tests reject insufficient observations, invalid shapes, nonfinite or
nonbinary outcomes, one-class samples, dependent columns, and selected complete
and quasi-separated designs. They check scaled predictor units, stable arithmetic
at extreme logits, iteration exhaustion, missing-row warnings and alignment.
OLS integration tests also run after changes to the shared PHP conversion code.
No penalties or Firth correction are supplied. The separation check is not an
exhaustive LP detector, and Wald inference can be poor with sparse or near-separated
samples. Linux and PHP-FPM deployment have not been exercised by these reports.

## Reproduce

From the repository root with matching PHP development tools:

```sh
export PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php
export PHP_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/bin/php-config
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
php -n -d "extension=$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib" tests/logistic.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_logistic.py
QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python" quarto render docs/notebooks/logistic-verification.qmd
```

Use `.so` on Linux. R fixture regeneration is an explicit development step:
`Rscript tests/generate-logistic-fixtures.R`. Ordinary Rust/PHP tests use saved
fixtures without R or Python. See [development](../development.qmd) for setup and
[large-sample benchmarks](../benchmarks/logistic.qmd) for additional evidence.
